title: The Blue Line: A Stewardship Instrument for Maintained Commitments
description: A stewardship instrument for maintained commitments: systems, obligations, and relationships to past work. It reads a declared file of commitments against a versioned registry and returns a fail-closed declaration-coverage verdict (MAINTAINED, NEEDS_ATTENTION, STALE, OUTSIDE_SCOPE) over the care signals each commitment requires. It measures whether the care a steward declared was fresh at the review date — never whether the care happened; a MAINTAINED verdict is not a warranty, SLA, availability guarantee, or proof of maintenance, and it never authorizes an action. License: Apache-2.0. See LICENSE in the repository.

methods.name: Versioned registry of twelve commitments with SHA-256 digest pinning
methods.description: Commitments are frozen records (id, title, wire, tags, required care signals, kind) whose sorted canonical form is hashed and pinned in every reading.
methods.evidence: The registry lists twelve commitments, each a frozen record with an id, a title, a wire (the practice in one sentence), applicable tags from a reviewed vocabulary, an ordered tuple of required care signals, and a kind family

methods.name: Staged, fail-closed intake normalization of declared files
methods.description: Declared files are normalized; malformed tags or undated signals are set aside as intake notes rather than causing crashes or invented values.
methods.evidence: dated care signals must carry ISO dates or they are set aside with notes. Nothing crashes and nothing is invented: every ignored token becomes an intake note the declarer can read.

methods.name: Freshness-window evaluation into MAINTAINED / NEEDS_ATTENTION / STALE
methods.description: Required signals of tag-matched commitments are compared with signals declared within a freshness window (180 days by default) to assign a verdict.
methods.evidence: All fresh yields MAINTAINED; some missing yields NEEDS_ATTENTION; a missing signal that aged past the window yields STALE.

methods.name: Formal definition of readings, commitments and fresh sets
methods.description: A reading is formalised as a tuple and properties (fail-closed, staleness monotonicity, digest pinning) are stated.
methods.evidence: A reading is a tuple 𝑅= (𝑣, 𝐹, 𝑁, 𝑑, 𝑔) where 𝑣is the file verdict, 𝐹is a tuple of commitment findings, 𝑁is a tuple of intake notes, 𝑑is the review date, and 𝑔is the registry digest.

methods.name: Worked examples: maintained quarter, stale repository, unmatched scan
methods.description: Three illustrative declared files show the verdicts the instrument returns; these are examples, not an empirical evaluation.
methods.evidence: The same file with every signal dated 2025-01-01, read at 2026-08-01. Every signal is older than the 180-day window, so the applicable commitments read STALE and the file verdict is STALE.

key_findings: An empty scan set (no matching commitment or unreadable file) returns OUTSIDE_SCOPE with notes and never yields MAINTAINED.
The stated staleness-monotonicity property holds that the stale set is always a subset of the missing set.
The verdict is a declaration-coverage statement, explicitly not a warranty, SLA, availability guarantee or proof of maintenance.
The author notes the instrument only reads declarations and does not inspect repositories, run checks or contact anyone; the freshness window is a policy constant, not empirical.
key_findings_evidence: Fail-closed property. If no commitment applies to the declared file, the verdict is $v = $ OUTSIDE_SCOPE and 𝐹is empty. An empty scan never yields MAINTAINED.
If a signal label is in the stale set at date 𝑑, it is in the missing set for every commitment requiring it; stale is always a subset of missing.
The verdict is a declaration-coverage statement and never a warranty, SLA, availability guarantee, or proof of maintenance.
It does not inspect repositories, run checks, or contact anyone whose obligation is recorded. • The freshness window is a policy constant, not an empirical threshold.
